title: Mind the (Belief) Gap: Group Identity in the World of LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Simulating the classical Rokeach and Mezei (1966) psychology experiments by having LLM agents interact with confederates who either agree or disagree on various campus and field discussion topics, then measuring their preference for choosing partners with shared beliefs.

Measuring the spread of misinformation in politically homogeneous vs. heterogeneous multi-agent groups (Democrat vs. Republican), and evaluating whether agents prefer to learn from and trust politically aligned sources over more accurate but politically unaligned sources in a pattern recognition task.

Assigning Black and White racial identities to confederate agents in the belief congruence simulation to evaluate whether LLMs prioritize shared beliefs over racial group membership when selecting conversation or work partners.
Conducting demographic ablations by replacing racial identities with gender identities to test whether the LLM's preference for shared beliefs outweighs gender homophily.
Conducting demographic ablations by assigning different age groups to agents to observe if belief congruence remains a stronger determinant of agent preference than age-based identity.
